children: Intel Corporation (NASDAQ:INTC) reported a $2.1B Q2 operating loss yet unveiled three AI chips and improving 14A/18A yields as it pursues HBM base‑die deals and foundry growth; shares fell after a large offering while analysts see AI CPUs and packaging gains as key to future recovery.
Intel Posts $2.1B Loss; HBM Contract Talks
: Intel (INTC) posted a $2.1B operating loss in Q2 2026; talks underway on a potential HBM base-die contract that could involve Intel Foundry Services to boost its contract-manufacturing efforts.
: Intel (INTC) revealed three AI chips at Hot Chips 2026: Diamond Rapids—up to 256 cores, 16 memory channels; Crescent Island—low‑power inference for data centers; Wildcat Lake—for laptops/edge AI.
: Intel (INTC) slid up to 5.47% to $85.14 amid a semiconductor sell-off ahead of Nvidia results. Shares fell below the $95 secondary offering price after a $20B, ~210.5M‑share sale.
: Intel (INTC) says 14A defect density is improving, 18A yields are ahead of targets, 14A PDK v0.9 due in October, risk production slated for 2027 and HVM targeted for 2028
: GF Securities raised Intel (INTC) back-end revenue forecasts to $1.1B for FY2027 and $7B for FY2028, citing improved visibility in Intel's AI packaging programs.
Intel May Benefit From Foundry Progress

: Intel (INTC) may benefit from a bigger server CPU market and progress in its foundry buildout to win external customers; analysts stress future results hinge on server execution and foundry advances.
Raymond James: AI CPUs Boost Demand
: Raymond James sees CPU market near $201B by 2030; AI-driven CPUs to boost demand. Notes rising competition and AMD’s AI CPU push could pressure Intel Corporation (INTC) market share.
